Give a filing's facts their names, place and sign convention

Source: R/add_taxonomy.R
add_taxonomy.Rd

Joins facts from read_xbrl() to the taxonomy they declare, so every reported figure arrives with the statement it belongs to, a stable accounting code, its Danish label, whether it is debit or credit, and whether it is the group's figure or the parent company's.

Usage

add_taxonomy(x, taxonomy = NULL, dimensions = TRUE)

Arguments

x

A tibble from read_xbrl().

taxonomy

A cvrr_taxonomy from read_taxonomy(), or a list of them. NULL, the default, uses the taxonomies packaged with cvrr – see cvrr_taxonomy_tables – which covers 20121001 to 20251001 and needs nothing on disk. Pass a package only for a taxonomy those do not hold.

dimensions

If TRUE (default), each dimension present in the data gets its own column holding the member that applies, named dim_ plus the dimension's local name – dim_ClassesOfPropertyPlantAndEquipment, dim_ConsolidatedSolo. The prefix is how check_breakdown() finds them again without having to guess.

Value

x with statement, code, depth, label, is_total, is_leaf, balance, periodtype, basis, basis_source, is_line (whether the fact is the statement line itself rather than a breakdown of it) and period added.

Details

read_xbrl() calls this itself unless told not to. Reach for it directly when the filings need a taxonomy package the cvrr tables do not hold, or when the facts were read once and are to be joined more than one way.

The join key is the namespace, not the prefix

Filers bind namespace prefixes freely – d, e, f, g, EOGS_202040000 all appear – and the same letter means different namespaces in different filings. Joining on the prefix looks equivalent and silently attaches the wrong element definition, so the join runs on the namespace URI.

Parent company versus group

Consolidated figures are tagged with a member of ConsolidatedSoloDimension. Parent-company figures are not tagged at all, and reading their absence as "parent" is only legitimate because the taxonomy declares a default member for that dimension. This function reads the declared default rather than assuming one, and records in basis_source whether the filing said so ("tagged") or the default decided it ("default") – a figure that is the parent's only by default is worth being able to find again.

Codes

The code comes from the taxonomy's own numbering: the role URI gives the statement (.../role/400.00/BalanceSheetAccountForm) and the presentation arcs' order values give the levels, so 400.00.020.010.020 is "Assets, non-current, property plant and equipment" and sorts into statement order on its own.

Nothing is dropped

A fact keeps its row whether or not the taxonomy has anything to say about it. Two kinds do not:

  • Facts in no statement – company data, the management's review, the auditor's report. They are the whole of what xbrl_company() reads, so dropping them would mean reading every filing twice. They come back with statement NA.

  • Facts whose taxonomy version is unknown, because the filing declares an entry point newer than the packaged tables. Every taxonomy column is NA and one warning names the version, so a filing from a taxonomy this release has not caught up with degrades to its raw facts instead of disappearing. read_taxonomy() on the published package fixes it.

One row per statement

An element belongs to every statement that presents it, and many do: ProfitLoss is the income statement's bottom line, the figure the proposed distribution starts from, and a key figure. A fact therefore comes back once per statement it appears in. Filter on statement before working with a statement, and never sum across them.

See also

read_xbrl(), which calls this by default, xbrl_accounts() for the tables built on top of it, read_taxonomy().

Other taxonomy: check_breakdown(), check_cascade(), check_continuity(), check_inclusion(), check_movement(), check_statement(), read_taxonomy(), xbrl_accounts(), xbrl_company(), xbrl_fill(), xbrl_lines(), xbrl_movements(), xbrl_note_tables(), xbrl_period(), xbrl_resolve()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# normally not needed -- read_xbrl() does it
x <- read_xbrl("materiale/xbrl", taxonomy = FALSE)
x <- add_taxonomy(x)

# a taxonomy version the packaged tables do not cover
add_taxonomy(x, read_taxonomy("XBRL20251001.zip"))
} # }
